description:
A non-pressured collection can size to-space below live data and panic with "Cheney: to-space exhausted" (runtime/src/heap/gc/forward.rs). The attached probe reaches it through gifts alone: a receiver with 2000 survivors in a 192768-byte block allocates 82000 live bytes (below its 96384 threshold), adopts 15360 bytes of gifts, and the SHRINK band sizes to-space at 28160 for 97360 live bytes.

The cause is two accountings that disagree. The pressure flag (note_alloc_pressure, graft, end_gift) is raised from bytes_used = own footprint + adopted fill + fragment bytes. The band decision in gc_with_extra_roots reconstructs the trigger as was_pressured = any abandoned block || own footprint >= threshold, which ignores adopted and fragment bytes. When the flag was raised by bytes the band cannot see, the GC believes it is unpressured, lands in SHRINK, and never looks at the live own fill since the last pass. Nothing enforces the one invariant Cheney needs: to-space capacity >= bytes that can be copied.

BEAM (erl_gc.c, local checkout ../otp) has one counter for everything outside the heap (mbuf_sz), a trigger that is a predicate over state (ERTS_IS_GC_DESIRED), and a sizer that starts from copyable bytes (young_gen_usage) before any policy applies. The fold adopts that shape.

Done when:
- abandoned_blocks and adopted_blocks are one Vec<Block>, counted by fill. own_footprint, adopted_fill, bytes_used's three-term sum and the "adopted blocks take no part in the band decision" rule are gone. GcStats.adopted_blocks and adopted_bytes are deleted (they have no jsonl consumer; fz.runtime.send.probe already carries gift_bytes and gift_blocks).
- Heap::should_gc is a pure function of heap state (tip fill + block fill, plus fragment bytes until the fragment ticket lands, against block_size / 2). The AtomicBool pressure field, note_alloc_pressure, clear_should_gc_flag and the three scheduler sites that clear it (process.rs boundary_maintenance, aot_shim.rs dispatch, ir_codegen/compiled.rs) are deleted. end_gift and graft no longer compute pressure.
- gc_with_extra_roots computes copyable = tip fill + block fill first. to_size is at least pick_size_class(copyable). The bands (GROW / SHRINK / KEEP) choose between that floor and a larger size; was_pressured is gone and GROW is decided from copyable versus block_size, not from the trigger. The band comment states the floor as its first sentence.
- One address-range iterator (tip, saved gift tip, blocks) backs contains_heap_addr, HeapView::contains and ptr_in_from_space; the three predicates become one.
- The attached probe, with the clear_should_gc_flag line removed, is the regression test in gift_test.rs: gifts alone make should_gc true, and the collection succeeds with to_space_capacity_bytes >= live bytes. A second test does the same through own allocation with no gifts and a direct gc call.
- Existing pins hold unchanged: thousands_of_small_unread_gifts_leave_the_receivers_size_class_unchanged_after_gc, gc_sizes_to_fit_and_never_shrinks_below_live_as_load_grows, gc_keeps_arena_bounded_across_many_cycles, and the fz.runtime.gc size_class pins in the fixture matrix. Any pin that moves is reported with its before and after value, not edited.
- Tests that poke gc_threshold_bytes to force a collection (heap_test.rs:779, heap_test.rs:1630) instead force it through state (a small heap) or call gc directly.
- Full gate green. Commit in Why / What changed / Verification form. No co-author trailer.

Tests: the two regression tests above (must fail on the parent commit, pass after), plus a test that should_gc is false immediately after a collection with no further allocation and true after enough allocation, with no clear call in between.
title: The collect-now predicate and the to-space size read one copyable-bytes figure
